value.overview: The California Condor (Gymnogyps californianus) is a vulture recorded in the United States. Field recognition often comes from huge wingspan, black body, white underwing patches, bare orange-pink head, and soaring flight. In the U.S. source data, it appeared in 3 state or DC summaries, including AZ, CA, UT. It is most associated with Aridlands:  Chaparral and Forests:  Temperate Western, and local season should be checked before trip planning.
value.classification: The California Condor belongs to the family New World Vultures in the order Cathartiformes. This is the practical birding classification used for the BirdIntel profile cache.
value.identification: Look for huge wingspan, black body, white underwing patches, bare orange-pink head, and soaring flight. Also use size, posture, flight style, voice, behavior, habitat, and season. Plumage can vary by sex, age, molt, and light, so the safest identification comes from combining several field marks rather than relying on one color or feature.
